records.source: וַיְדַבֵּ֥ר יְהוָ֖ה אֶל־מֹשֶׁ֥ה לֵּאמֹֽר׃
records.gloss: And spoke Yahweh to Moses, saying,
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} said to Moses,

L.1: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} spoke to Moses, saying,

decisions.choice: Yahweh spoke: the word about the firstborn follows the night of the exodus
decisions.reason: These instructions come straight after the account of the night when Egypt's firstborn died and Israel went out (12:29-51). Israel's firstborn were spared that night, and God now claims them (verse 2; verse 15).

records.heading: Firstborn and unleavened bread

records.source: קַדֶּשׁ־לִ֨י כָל־בְּכ֜וֹר פֶּ֤טֶר כָּל־רֶ֨חֶם֙ בִּבְנֵ֣י יִשְׂרָאֵ֔ל בָּאָדָ֖ם וּבַבְּהֵמָ֑ה לִ֖י הֽוּא׃
records.gloss: Consecrate to me every firstborn, [the] opening of every womb among [the] sons of Israel, among humankind and among livestock; to me it [is].
pieces: "Set apart as holy to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} every firstborn among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, each one that comes first from its mother's womb, human and animal alike. It belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}."

L.2: "Consecrate to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} every firstborn, the first to open every womb among the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel, of man and of beast; it [is] {{deity_pronoun:mine|Mine}}."

R.2: "Set apart for {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}} every firstborn male. Among the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}}, the first male born to each mother belongs to {{deity_pronoun:me|Me}}, whether a child or an animal."

decisions.choice: consecrate ... it is mine: the firstborn belong to God
decisions.reason: To consecrate is to make holy, to set something apart as God's own. On the night of the tenth plague God struck Egypt's firstborn and spared Israel's (12:12-13, 29). From then on Israel's firstborn belong to him (verse 15; Numbers 3:13; 8:17). Israel itself is God's firstborn son (4:22).

decisions.choice: the opening of every womb: the first child a mother bears
decisions.reason: The phrase means the first to be born from a mother, human or animal. Verses 12 and 15 make clear that the males are meant.

decisions.choice: set apart as holy
decisions.reason: Balanced says what "consecrate" means; Literal keeps the word.

decisions.choice: firstborn male ... first male born to each mother
decisions.reason: Readable says "male" because verses 12 and 15 say so, and explains "the opening of the womb".

records.source: וַיֹּ֨אמֶר מֹשֶׁ֜ה אֶל־הָעָ֗ם זָכ֞וֹר אֶת־הַיּ֤וֹם הַזֶּה֙ אֲשֶׁ֨ר יְצָאתֶ֤ם מִמִּצְרַ֨יִם֙ מִבֵּ֣ית עֲבָדִ֔ים כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִ֧יא יְהֹוָ֛ה אֶתְכֶ֖ם מִזֶּ֑ה וְלֹ֥א יֵאָכֵ֖ל חָמֵֽץ׃
records.gloss: And said Moses to the people, remember this day on which you went out from Egypt, from [a] house of slaves, for by strength of hand brought out Yahweh you from this [place]; and not shall be eaten leavened [bread].
pieces: Moses said to the people, "Remember this day, the day you came out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out of this place by the strength of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand. No leavened bread may be eaten.

L.3: And Moses said to the people, "Remember this day on which you went out from Egypt, from the house of slaves, for by strength of hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out from here; and nothing leavened shall be eaten.

R.3: Moses told the people, "Always remember this day. It is the day you left Egypt, where you were slaves. {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring you out. Do not eat any bread made with yeast.

decisions.choice: the house of slaves: Egypt, the place where Israel was enslaved
decisions.reason: Egypt is pictured as a house of slavery, a place where Israel lived as slaves. The phrase returns in verse 14 and at the opening of the Ten Commandments (20:2; Deuteronomy 5:6).

decisions.choice: by strength of hand: by force, by God's power
decisions.reason: The hand stands for power. God said that Pharaoh would let Israel go only under a strong hand (3:19; 6:1). The phrase returns in verses 9, 14 and 16.

decisions.choice: leavened bread: bread made with leaven, which makes dough rise
decisions.reason: As in 12:15 and 12:19-20. Leaven was a piece of fermented dough kept from an earlier batch and mixed into new dough.

decisions.choice: his hand (Balanced); used his great power (Readable)
decisions.reason: The hand is God's, so Balanced says "his hand" and Readable says what the picture means. Literal keeps "by strength of hand".

decisions.choice: bread made with yeast
decisions.reason: Readable uses the familiar word "yeast" for leaven.

decisions.choice: house of slaves / slavery; slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" and "slavery" at every level, as the style guide keeps them for Israel's slavery in Egypt, "the house of slavery" (m1).

records.source: הַיּ֖וֹם אַתֶּ֣ם יֹצְאִ֑ים בְּחֹ֖דֶשׁ הָאָבִֽיב׃
records.gloss: Today you [are] going out, in [the] month of the Abib.
pieces: You are going out today, in the month of Abib.

L.4: Today you are going out, in the month of Abib.

R.4: You are leaving today, in the month of Abib, in early spring.

decisions.choice: the month of Abib: the month of new ears of grain, March-April
decisions.reason: Abib means fresh ears of grain; the same word describes the barley in 9:31. It is the first month of the year (12:2), about March-April, when the barley was ripening. After the exile it was called Nisan (Nehemiah 2:1; Esther 3:7).

decisions.choice: in early spring
decisions.reason: Readable says when the month fell.

records.source: וְהָיָ֣ה כִֽי־יְבִֽיאֲךָ֣ יְהוָ֡ה אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽ֠כְּנַעֲנִי וְהַחִתִּ֨י וְהָאֱמֹרִ֜י וְהַחִוִּ֣י וְהַיְבוּסִ֗י אֲשֶׁ֨ר נִשְׁבַּ֤ע לַאֲבֹתֶ֨יךָ֙ לָ֣תֶת לָ֔ךְ אֶ֛רֶץ זָבַ֥ת חָלָ֖ב וּדְבָ֑שׁ וְעָבַדְתָּ֛ אֶת־הָעֲבֹדָ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את בַּחֹ֥דֶשׁ הַזֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it will be when brings you Yahweh into [the] land of the Canaanite and the Hittite and the Amorite and the Hivite and the Jebusite, which he swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing [with] milk and honey, and you shall serve this service in this month.
pieces: When {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings you into the land of the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites, the land {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your ancestors that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give you, a land flowing with milk and honey, you are to perform this rite in this same month.

L.5: And it shall be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings you into the land of the Canaanites and the Hittites and the Amorites and the Hivites and the Jebusites, which {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to your fathers to give to you, a land flowing [with] milk and honey, that you shall serve this service in this month.

R.5: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring you into the land where the Canaanites, Hittites, Amorites, Hivites, and Jebusites live. He promised your ancestors with an oath that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would give it to you. It is a rich land, full of milk and honey. When you are living there, you must keep this ceremony in this month.

decisions.choice: the land of the Canaanites ... flowing with milk and honey: the land promised in 3:8
decisions.reason: God named these peoples and described the land in the same words at the burning bush (3:8, 17). The list here has five names; the Perizzites of 3:8 are not mentioned. Milk and honey stand for a rich land; see the note at 3:8.

decisions.choice: serve this service: carry out this rite of worship
decisions.reason: The noun means work or service. It was used of Israel's hard labor as slaves in Egypt (1:14; 2:23); now it names the service Israel will give to God, as in 12:25-26.

decisions.choice: he swore to your fathers: the oath to the ancestors
decisions.reason: God promised the land on oath to Abraham, Isaac and Jacob (Genesis 15:18; 26:3; Exodus 6:8). Bringing Israel into it keeps that oath.

decisions.choice: ancestors; this rite (Balanced); this ceremony (Readable)
decisions.reason: "Fathers" means forefathers, so Balanced and Readable say "ancestors", as Readable does in 3:16. Literal keeps "serve this service" to show the repeated word.

records.source: שִׁבְעַ֥ת יָמִ֖ים תֹּאכַ֣ל מַצֹּ֑ת וּבַיּוֹם֙ הַשְּׁבִיעִ֔י חַ֖ג לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the day the seventh [there is a] festival to Yahweh.
pieces: You are to eat unleavened bread for seven days, and the seventh day is a feast in honor of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.6: Seven days you shall eat unleavened bread, and on the seventh day [there is] a feast to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.6: Eat unleavened bread for seven days. The seventh day is a festival to honor {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: seven days ... unleavened bread: the feast set out in 12:15-20
decisions.reason: Moses repeats the rule for the Feast of Unleavened Bread given in chapter 12. Unleavened bread is flat bread baked without leaven (12:39).

decisions.choice: feast: a pilgrimage festival
decisions.reason: The word is used for the great yearly feasts, when the people gathered to celebrate before God (10:9; 12:14; 23:14-17).

records.source: מַצּוֹת֙ יֵֽאָכֵ֔ל אֵ֖ת שִׁבְעַ֣ת הַיָּמִ֑ים וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֨ה לְךָ֜ חָמֵ֗ץ וְלֹֽא־יֵרָאֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ שְׂאֹ֖ר בְּכָל־גְּבֻלֶֽךָ׃
records.gloss: Unleavened bread shall be eaten [for] the seven days, and not shall be seen with you leavened [bread], and not shall be seen with you leaven in all your territory.
pieces: Throughout the seven days unleavened bread is to be eaten. No leavened bread may be found among you, and no leaven anywhere in all your territory.

L.7: Unleavened bread shall be eaten [for] the seven days; and nothing leavened shall be seen with you, and no leaven shall be seen with you in all your territory.

R.7: Eat unleavened bread during all seven days. There must be no bread made with yeast in your homes, and no yeast at all anywhere in your land.

decisions.choice: leavened bread ... leaven: the bread, and what makes it rise
decisions.reason: The first word is bread or food made with leaven; the second is the leaven itself, the sour dough kept to start a new batch (12:15, 19). Neither is to be kept during the feast.

decisions.choice: not be seen with you: not be found in your possession
decisions.reason: The point is not merely that it is out of sight, but that none is to be in the house or the land at all (12:19).

decisions.choice: in your homes ... in your land
decisions.reason: Readable says where the leaven must not be found; Balanced and Literal keep "with you" and "territory".

records.source: וְהִגַּדְתָּ֣ לְבִנְךָ֔ בַּיּ֥וֹם הַה֖וּא לֵאמֹ֑ר בַּעֲב֣וּר זֶ֗ה עָשָׂ֤ה יְהוָה֙ לִ֔י בְּצֵאתִ֖י מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, because of this [which] did Yahweh for me when I went out from Egypt.
pieces: On that day tell your son what it means: '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} acted for me when I left Egypt, and that is why we do this.'

L.8: And you shall tell your son on that day, saying, '[It is] because of what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did for me when I came out from Egypt.'

R.8: On that day, explain it to your son. Say, 'We keep this festival because of what {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} did for me when I came out of Egypt.'

decisions.choice: because of this: because of what Yahweh did for me
alternatives: it was for this that Yahweh acted for me
decisions.reason: The short phrase most naturally means that the feast is kept because of what God did. It can also be read the other way round: God acted for me so that I would keep this feast and serve him.

decisions.choice: for me, when I came out: each generation speaks as one who came out
decisions.reason: The father speaks in the first person even in later generations, when he himself was not in Egypt. The story is passed on as the family's own (Deuteronomy 6:20-23). This verse is read in the Jewish Passover service.

decisions.choice: what it means / we do this; We keep this festival
decisions.reason: The Hebrew leaves "this" unexplained; it is the feast. Balanced and Readable say so.

records.source: וְהָיָה֩ לְךָ֨ לְא֜וֹת עַל־יָדְךָ֗ וּלְזִכָּרוֹן֙ בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֔יךָ לְמַ֗עַן תִּהְיֶ֛ה תּוֹרַ֥ת יְהוָ֖ה בְּפִ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּיָ֣ד חֲזָקָ֔ה הוֹצִֽאֲךָ֥ יְהֹוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And it shall be to you for a sign on your hand and for a memorial between your eyes, so that may be [the] law of Yahweh in your mouth; for by a strong hand brought you out Yahweh from Egypt.
pieces: This feast will be a sign for you, like a mark on your hand, and a reminder, like a mark between your eyes, so that the instruction of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} stays on your lips. For with a strong hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out of Egypt.

L.9: And it shall be to you for a sign on your hand and for a memorial between your eyes, so that the law of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} may be in your mouth; for with a strong hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out from Egypt.

R.9: This festival will remind you of what happened, like a mark on your hand or on your forehead that you see every day. It will help you keep talking about the teaching of {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}. For {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought you out of Egypt with {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power.

decisions.choice: a sign on your hand and a memorial between your eyes: a constant reminder
alternatives: a command to wear a physical sign
decisions.reason: Here the feast itself is the sign: keeping it every year reminds Israel of the exodus as surely as a mark on the hand or the forehead would. Compare Proverbs 3:3 and 6:21. Later Jewish practice took the words literally: phylacteries, small boxes holding written passages (among them 13:1-10 and 13:11-16), are worn on the arm and the forehead, following this verse, verse 16, Deuteronomy 6:8 and 11:18 (compare Matthew 23:5).

decisions.choice: the law of Yahweh: Yahweh's instruction, his teaching
decisions.reason: The word means instruction or teaching. Here it is first of all God's instruction about this feast and the story it tells; it later names the whole law given through Moses.

decisions.choice: in your mouth: spoken, talked about, recited
decisions.reason: What is in the mouth is said and repeated (Deuteronomy 30:14; Joshua 1:8).

decisions.choice: like a mark on your hand ... between your eyes (Balanced); on your forehead that you see every day (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable mark the sign as a comparison, since here it is the feast that reminds. Literal keeps the picture as it stands.

decisions.choice: instruction ... on your lips (Balanced); teaching ... keep talking about (Readable)
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say "instruction" or "teaching" for the Hebrew word, since "law" here does not yet mean a code of laws. Literal keeps "law".

records.source: וְשָׁמַרְתָּ֛ אֶת־הַחֻקָּ֥ה הַזֹּ֖את לְמוֹעֲדָ֑הּ מִיָּמִ֖ים יָמִֽימָה׃ס
records.gloss: And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time from days to days.
pieces: So you are to keep this statute at its proper time every year.

L.10: And you shall keep this statute at its appointed time from days to days.

R.10: Keep this rule at the right time every year.

decisions.choice: from days to days: year after year
decisions.reason: "Days" here stands for a year, as in Judges 11:40 and 1 Samuel 1:3.

decisions.choice: statute: a fixed and lasting rule
decisions.reason: The word names a rule that is set and must be kept for good, as in 12:14, 17.

decisions.choice: rule
decisions.reason: Readable says "rule" for "statute".

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־יְבִֽאֲךָ֤ יְהוָה֙ אֶל־אֶ֣רֶץ הַֽכְּנַעֲנִ֔י כַּאֲשֶׁ֛ר נִשְׁבַּ֥ע לְךָ֖ וְלַֽאֲבֹתֶ֑יךָ וּנְתָנָ֖הּ לָֽךְ׃
records.gloss: And it shall be when brings you Yahweh into [the] land of the Canaanite, as he swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,
pieces: Once {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} has brought you into the land of the Canaanites and handed it over to you, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} would to you and to your ancestors,

L.11: And it shall be, when {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brings you into the land of the Canaanites, as {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} swore to you and to your fathers, and gives it to you,

R.11: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} will bring you into the land of the Canaanites and give it to you. He promised this with an oath to you and to your ancestors.

decisions.choice: the land of the Canaanite: the land of all the peoples named in verse 5
decisions.reason: The Canaanites stand here for all the peoples of the land, who are listed in verse 5.

decisions.choice: he swore to you and to your fathers: the promise includes this generation
decisions.reason: The oath was given to the ancestors (Genesis 15:18; 26:3), but it counts as made to the Israelites now leaving Egypt as well.

decisions.choice: ancestors
decisions.reason: As in verse 5.

records.heading: Redeeming the firstborn

records.source: וְהַעֲבַרְתָּ֥ כָל־פֶּֽטֶר־רֶ֖חֶם לַֽיהֹוָ֑ה וְכָל־פֶּ֣טֶר׀שֶׁ֣גֶר בְּהֵמָ֗ה אֲשֶׁ֨ר יִהְיֶ֥ה לְךָ֛ הַזְּכָרִ֖ים לַיהוָֽה׃
records.gloss: that you shall make pass over every opener of [the] womb to Yahweh, and every firstling, offspring of livestock which will be to you, the males [are] to Yahweh.
pieces: then you must hand over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every firstborn that opens the womb. Every firstling born to your animals that is a male belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

L.12: that you shall hand over to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every first opener of the womb; and every firstling, the young of livestock that you have, the males [belong] to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

R.12: Then you must give to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every firstborn male. The first male born to each of your animals belongs to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}}.

decisions.choice: make pass over: hand over, give up to Yahweh
decisions.reason: The verb means to cause something to pass to another, as an inheritance passes to an heir (Numbers 27:7-8). The firstborn are transferred to God as his own.

decisions.choice: the young of livestock: the first young of cattle, sheep and goats
decisions.reason: The word for the young of animals is rare (Deuteronomy 7:13). Every first male born to the herds and flocks belongs to God.

decisions.choice: the males: only the males are given
decisions.reason: "The males" limits the rule: the firstborn males belong to Yahweh (verse 15; Deuteronomy 15:19).

records.source: וְכָל־פֶּ֤טֶר חֲמֹר֙ תִּפְדֶּ֣ה בְשֶׂ֔ה וְאִם־לֹ֥א תִפְדֶּ֖ה וַעֲרַפְתּ֑וֹ וְכֹ֨ל בְּכ֥וֹר אָדָ֛ם בְּבָנֶ֖יךָ תִּפְדֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And every firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if not you redeem [it], then you shall break its neck. And every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.
pieces: Every firstborn donkey you are to redeem by giving a lamb in its place; if you will not redeem it, you must break its neck. And you are to redeem every firstborn son of yours.

L.13: And every firstling of a donkey you shall redeem with a lamb, and if you do not redeem [it], you shall break its neck. And every firstborn of man among your sons you shall redeem.

R.13: You must buy back each firstborn donkey by giving a lamb in its place. If you do not buy it back, you must break its neck. You must also buy back each of your firstborn sons.

decisions.choice: a donkey redeemed with a lamb, or its neck broken
decisions.reason: A donkey could not be offered in sacrifice, so a lamb or young goat was given in its place (Numbers 18:15). If the owner would not do that, the donkey was killed: he could not keep for himself an animal that belonged to God. The word for lamb means one young animal of the flock, sheep or goat (12:5).

decisions.choice: redeem: buy back by paying a price in its place
decisions.reason: To redeem is to free something that belongs to another by paying for it. Firstborn sons were bought back from God; later the price was set at five shekels (Numbers 3:46-47; 18:16).

decisions.choice: every firstborn among your sons: never sacrificed, always redeemed
decisions.reason: Israel's firstborn sons belong to God, but he does not take them as sacrifices; they are bought back. Later the Levites take their place (Numbers 3:12-13).

decisions.choice: buy back
decisions.reason: Readable says what "redeem" means.

records.source: וְהָיָ֞ה כִּֽי־יִשְׁאָלְךָ֥ בִנְךָ֛ מָחָ֖ר לֵאמֹ֣ר מַה־זֹּ֑את וְאָמַרְתָּ֣ אֵלָ֔יו בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֗ד הוֹצִיאָ֧נוּ יְהוָ֛ה מִמִּצְרַ֖יִם מִבֵּ֥ית עֲבָדִֽים׃
records.gloss: And it shall be when asks you your son in time to come, saying, what [is] this? then you shall say to him, by strength of hand brought us out Yahweh from Egypt, from [a] house of slaves.
pieces: Later on, when your son asks you, 'What is this?' you shall answer him, 'By the strength of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out of Egypt, out of the house of slavery.

L.14: And it shall be, when your son asks you in time to come, saying, 'What [is] this?' that you shall say to him, 'By strength of hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out from Egypt, from the house of slaves.

R.14: In the future your son will ask you, 'Why do we do this?' Then tell him, '{{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring us out of Egypt, where we were slaves.

decisions.choice: tomorrow: in time to come
decisions.reason: The word means "tomorrow", but here, as in Joshua 4:6 and 21, it means some time in the future.

decisions.choice: when your son asks, "What is this?": the teaching of children
decisions.reason: The same question and answer are found in 12:26-27, Deuteronomy 6:20-25 and Joshua 4:6-7. The rites are kept so that children will ask and the story will be told.

decisions.choice: his hand (Balanced); used his great power (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 3.

decisions.choice: Why do we do this?
decisions.reason: The son asks what the rite means; Readable puts the question as a child would.

decisions.choice: house of slaves / slavery; slaves
decisions.reason: "Slaves" and "slavery" at every level, as the style guide keeps them for Israel's slavery in Egypt, "the house of slavery" (verse 3).

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י כִּֽי־הִקְשָׁ֣ה פַרְעֹה֮ לְשַׁלְּחֵנוּ֒ וַיַּהֲרֹ֨ג יְהֹוָ֤ה כָּל־בְּכוֹר֙ בְּאֶ֣רֶץ מִצְרַ֔יִם מִבְּכֹ֥ר אָדָ֖ם וְעַד־בְּכ֣וֹר בְּהֵמָ֑ה עַל־כֵּן֩ אֲנִ֨י זֹבֵ֜חַ לַֽיהוָ֗ה כָּל־פֶּ֤טֶר רֶ֨חֶם֙ הַזְּכָרִ֔ים וְכָל־בְּכ֥וֹר בָּנַ֖י אֶפְדֶּֽה׃
records.gloss: And it was when made hard Pharaoh to let us go, then killed Yahweh every firstborn in [the] land of Egypt, from [the] firstborn of man and to [the] firstborn of beast. Therefore I sacrifice to Yahweh every opener of [the] womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.
pieces: When Pharaoh hardened himself against letting us go, {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, the firstborn of people and of animals alike. So I offer to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} in sacrifice every male that first opens the womb, and I redeem each firstborn among my sons.'

L.15: And it was, when Pharaoh made [it] hard to let us go, that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} killed every firstborn in the land of Egypt, from the firstborn of man to the firstborn of beast. Therefore I sacrifice to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} every opener of the womb, the males, and every firstborn of my sons I redeem.'

R.15: Pharaoh was stubborn and would not let us go. So {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} killed every firstborn in Egypt, both people and animals. That is the reason I offer every firstborn male animal to {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} as a sacrifice. But I buy back each of my firstborn sons.'

decisions.choice: Pharaoh made hard: Pharaoh made himself stubborn
decisions.reason: The verb is the one used for hardening in 7:3, here with Pharaoh as the one who hardens; the object, himself or his heart, is understood. See the note at 7:3.

decisions.choice: Yahweh killed ... therefore I sacrifice ... I redeem: why the firstborn belong to God
decisions.reason: Because God struck Egypt's firstborn and spared Israel's, the firstborn of Israel are his: the animals are sacrificed, and the sons are bought back (Numbers 3:13; 8:17).

decisions.choice: the father's answer ends here
decisions.reason: The Hebrew has no quotation marks. The answer begun in verse 14 most naturally ends with this verse; verse 16 returns to Moses' words, which echo verse 9. The answer could also run through verse 16.

decisions.choice: hardened himself (Balanced); was stubborn (Readable)
decisions.reason: As settled at 7:3. Literal keeps "made [it] hard".

decisions.choice: every firstborn male animal
decisions.reason: Readable makes clear that the sacrifice is of animals, since the sons are bought back.

records.source: וְהָיָ֤ה לְאוֹת֙ עַל־יָ֣דְכָ֔ה וּלְטוֹטָפֹ֖ת בֵּ֣ין עֵינֶ֑יךָ כִּ֚י בְּחֹ֣זֶק יָ֔ד הוֹצִיאָ֥נוּ יְהוָ֖ה מִמִּצְרָֽיִם׃ס
records.gloss: And it shall be for a sign on your hand and for frontlets between your eyes, for by strength of hand brought us out Yahweh from Egypt.
pieces: It will be a sign for you, like a mark on your hand and a band between your eyes, for by the strength of {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out of Egypt."

L.16: And it shall be for a sign on your hand and for frontlets between your eyes, for by strength of hand {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} brought us out from Egypt."

R.16: This practice will be like a mark on your hand or a band on your forehead. It will remind you that {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} used {{deity_pronoun:his|His}} great power to bring us out of Egypt."

decisions.choice: frontlets: a band or mark worn on the forehead
decisions.reason: The word is found only here and in Deuteronomy 6:8 and 11:18, and its meaning is not certain. It may be a headband, an ornament, or a mark on the forehead. In verse 9 the matching word is "memorial". On the later practice of phylacteries see the note at verse 9.

decisions.choice: a sign on your hand ... by strength of hand: verse 9 repeated
decisions.reason: The verse repeats verse 9, closing the instructions about the firstborn as verse 9 closed those about the feast.

decisions.choice: like a mark ... a band (Balanced); It will remind you that (Readable)
decisions.reason: As in verse 9, Balanced and Readable mark the sign as a comparison; Readable says what it reminds of.

records.source: וַיְהִ֗י בְּשַׁלַּ֣ח פַּרְעֹה֮ אֶת־הָעָם֒ וְלֹא־נָחָ֣ם אֱלֹהִ֗ים דֶּ֚רֶךְ אֶ֣רֶץ פְּלִשְׁתִּ֔ים כִּ֥י קָר֖וֹב ה֑וּא כִּ֣י׀אָמַ֣ר אֱלֹהִ֗ים פֶּֽן־יִנָּחֵ֥ם הָעָ֛ם בִּרְאֹתָ֥ם מִלְחָמָ֖ה וְשָׁ֥בוּ מִצְרָֽיְמָה׃
records.gloss: And it was when let go Pharaoh the people, and not led them God [by the] way of [the] land of [the] Philistines, for near [was] it; for said God, lest regret the people when they see war and they return to Egypt.
pieces: Once Pharaoh had sent the people away, God did not guide them along the route to the land of the Philistines, though it was the nearer way. For God thought, "The people may regret leaving when they find themselves facing war, and go back to Egypt."

L.17: And it was, when Pharaoh let the people go, that God did not lead them [by] the way of the land of the Philistines, for it [was] near; for God said, "Lest the people change [their] mind when they see war, and return to Egypt."

R.17: Pharaoh finally let the people go. The shortest way to Canaan went through the land of the Philistines, but God did not lead them that way. God thought, "If the people have to fight a war, they might be sorry they left and go back to Egypt."

decisions.choice: the way of the land of the Philistines: the coast road from Egypt to Canaan
decisions.reason: The main road from Egypt to Canaan ran along the Mediterranean coast, through the land later held by the Philistines. Egypt guarded it with a line of forts.

decisions.choice: for it was near: though it was the shorter way
decisions.reason: The word can give a reason or make a contrast. Most likely it is a contrast: God did not lead them that way, even though it was nearer. It may instead give the reason: because it was near, the people would soon meet war.

decisions.choice: God said ... lest the people regret: God thought, the people may change their minds
decisions.reason: "Said" here means said to himself, thought. The verb means to be sorry or to change one's mind: faced with war, the people might wish they had never left (compare 14:11-12; Numbers 14:3-4).

decisions.choice: The shortest way to Canaan
decisions.reason: Readable says where the road led and what "near" means.

records.heading: The pillar of cloud and fire

records.source: וַיַּסֵּ֨ב אֱלֹהִ֧ים׀אֶת־הָעָ֛ם דֶּ֥רֶךְ הַמִּדְבָּ֖ר יַם־ס֑וּף וַחֲמֻשִׁ֛ים עָל֥וּ בְנֵי־יִשְׂרָאֵ֖ל מֵאֶ֥רֶץ מִצְרָֽיִם׃
records.gloss: And led around God the people [by the] way of the wilderness [to the] Sea of Reeds; and equipped for battle went up [the] sons of Israel from [the] land of Egypt.
pieces: Instead, God took the people the long way round, through the wilderness toward the Red Sea, and the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left the land of Egypt equipped for battle.

L.18: And God led the people around [by] the way of the wilderness [toward] the Sea of Reeds; and the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel went up equipped for battle from the land of Egypt.

R.18: So God led them the long way, through the desert toward the Red Sea. The {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} left Egypt ready to fight.

decisions.choice: the Sea of Reeds: the sea Israel would cross, known as the Red Sea
decisions.reason: See the note at 10:19. This is the sea of the crossing in chapters 14-15.

decisions.choice: equipped for battle: armed, or in battle order
decisions.reason: The word is rare (Joshua 1:14; 4:12; Judges 7:11) and its meaning is not certain. It may mean armed, or drawn up in ranks for battle. Some link it to the number five, "in fifties" or "in five divisions". Israel left not as runaways but as an organized people (12:41, 51).

decisions.choice: the Red Sea
decisions.reason: As in 10:19: Balanced and Readable use the familiar name; Literal translates the Hebrew name, "Sea of Reeds".

records.source: וַיִּקַּ֥ח מֹשֶׁ֛ה אֶת־עַצְמ֥וֹת יוֹסֵ֖ף עִמּ֑וֹ כִּי֩ הַשְׁבֵּ֨עַ הִשְׁבִּ֜יעַ אֶת־בְּנֵ֤י יִשְׂרָאֵל֙ לֵאמֹ֔ר פָּקֹ֨ד יִפְקֹ֤ד אֱלֹהִים֙ אֶתְכֶ֔ם וְהַעֲלִיתֶ֧ם אֶת־עַצְמֹתַ֛י מִזֶּ֖ה אִתְּכֶֽם׃
records.gloss: And took Moses the bones of Joseph with him, for surely he had made swear the sons of Israel, saying, surely will visit God you, and you shall bring up my bones from here with you.
pieces: Moses brought Joseph's bones along, since Joseph had bound the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} by a solemn oath. "God will certainly come to help you," he had said, "and when {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, you are to take my bones up from here with you."

L.19: And Moses took the bones of Joseph with him, for he had surely made the {{gender:children|sons}} of Israel swear, saying, "God will surely visit you, and you shall bring up my bones from here with you."

R.19: Moses took the bones of Joseph along. Long before, Joseph had made the {{gender:Israelites|sons of Israel}} promise to do this. He had told them, "God will surely come to help you. When {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} does, carry my bones with you out of this land."

decisions.choice: the bones of Joseph: the oath of Genesis 50:25 is kept
decisions.reason: Before he died Joseph made his brothers swear to take his bones with them when God brought them out (Genesis 50:24-25). Moses keeps that oath; the bones were buried at Shechem (Joshua 24:32).

decisions.choice: God will surely visit you: God will come to your aid
decisions.reason: As in 3:16 and 4:31, the doubled verb means God will certainly come to help. Joseph's words are now fulfilled.

decisions.choice: he had surely made swear: a solemn oath
decisions.reason: The verb is doubled for emphasis: Joseph put them under a binding oath.

decisions.choice: Long before
decisions.reason: Readable says that the oath was made long ago, in Joseph's lifetime.

records.source: וַיִּסְע֖וּ מִסֻּכֹּ֑ת וַיַּחֲנ֣וּ בְאֵתָ֔ם בִּקְצֵ֖ה הַמִּדְבָּֽר׃
records.gloss: And they set out from Succoth and encamped at Etham, at [the] edge of the wilderness.
pieces: They moved on from Succoth and made camp at Etham, on the edge of the wilderness.

L.20: And they set out from Succoth and camped at Etham, at the edge of the wilderness.

R.20: The people left Succoth and set up camp at Etham, where the desert begins.

decisions.choice: Succoth ... Etham: the first stages of the journey
decisions.reason: Israel set out from Rameses to Succoth (12:37). Where Etham lay is not known, except that it was on the edge of the wilderness east of Egypt (Numbers 33:6-7).

records.source: וַֽיהוָ֡ה הֹלֵךְ֩ לִפְנֵיהֶ֨ם יוֹמָ֜ם בְּעַמּ֤וּד עָנָן֙ לַנְחֹתָ֣ם הַדֶּ֔רֶךְ וְלַ֛יְלָה בְּעַמּ֥וּד אֵ֖שׁ לְהָאִ֣יר לָהֶ֑ם לָלֶ֖כֶת יוֹמָ֥ם וָלָֽיְלָה׃
records.gloss: And Yahweh [was] going before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give light to them, to go by day and by night.
pieces: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} went in front of them, in a pillar of cloud by day so that {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} could guide them along the way, and in a pillar of fire by night to light their path. In that way they could keep moving both day and night.

L.21: And {{divine_name:the LORD|Yahweh}} was going before them by day in a pillar of cloud to lead them [on] the way, and by night in a pillar of fire to give them light, so that [they could] go by day and by night.

R.21: {{divine_name:The LORD|Yahweh}} went ahead of the people. During the day {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in a pillar of cloud to show them the way. At night {{deity_pronoun:he|He}} was in a pillar of fire to give them light. So they could travel in the daytime or at night.

decisions.choice: Yahweh was going before them: God himself present in the pillar
decisions.reason: The pillar is not only a sign; Yahweh himself goes with his people in it (14:19, 24; 33:9-10; Numbers 14:14). Cloud and fire mark his presence again at Sinai and at the tabernacle (19:18; 40:34-38).

decisions.choice: a pillar of cloud ... a pillar of fire: one column, seen as cloud by day and fire by night
decisions.reason: A pillar is a standing column. By day it looked like cloud, by night like fire (40:38; Numbers 9:15-16).

decisions.choice: so that he could guide them; he was in
decisions.reason: Balanced and Readable say that Yahweh is the one who guides and the one in the pillar.

records.source: לֹֽא־יָמִ֞ישׁ עַמּ֤וּד הֶֽעָנָן֙ יוֹמָ֔ם וְעַמּ֥וּד הָאֵ֖שׁ לָ֑יְלָה לִפְנֵ֖י הָעָֽם׃פ
records.gloss: Not departed [the] pillar of the cloud by day and [the] pillar of the fire by night from before the people.
pieces: By day the pillar of cloud, and by night the pillar of fire, never moved away from the front of the people.

L.22: The pillar of the cloud by day did not depart, nor the pillar of the fire by night, from before the people.

R.22: The pillar of cloud was always in front of the people during the day, and the pillar of fire was always there at night.

decisions.choice: did not depart: the pillar did not leave its place
alternatives: he did not remove the pillar
decisions.reason: The verb is most likely intransitive, with the pillar as its subject, as the same form is used of Joshua not leaving the tent in 33:11. It can also be read with Yahweh as the subject: "he did not take away the pillar of cloud by day or the pillar of fire by night".

decisions.choice: the pillar did not depart: God's unbroken presence
decisions.reason: God's guidance went with Israel all through the journey (40:38; Nehemiah 9:19).
